title: MEX of XOR
statementMd:
The nonempty prefix XORs of an array of length 𝑚m are the values 𝑎1⊕𝑎2⊕⋯⊕𝑎𝑘a1⊕a2⊕⋯⊕ak where 1≤𝑘≤𝑚1≤k≤m and ⊕⊕ denotes the bitwise XOR operation.

You are given an integer 𝑛n. Output a permutation∗∗ of the integers from 00 to 2𝑛−12n−1 such that the MEX†† of all nonempty prefix XORs is maximized.

∗∗A permutation of the integers from 00 to 2𝑛−12n−1 is an array consisting of 2𝑛2n distinct integers from 00 to 2𝑛−12n−1 in arbitrary order. For example, [2,3,1,0][2,3,1,0] is a permutation, but [1,1][1,1] is not a permutation (11 appears twice in the array), and [1,2,4,0][1,2,4,0] is also not a permutation (the length is 44 but there is 44 in the array).

††The minimum excluded (MEX) of a collection of integers 𝑐1,𝑐2,…,𝑐𝑘c1,c2,…,ck is defined as the smallest non-negative integer 𝑥x which does not occur in the collection 𝑐c.

## Input

The only line of input contains a single integer 𝑛n (2≤𝑛≤202≤n≤20).

## Output

Output 2𝑛2n integers which are a permutation such that the MEX of all nonempty prefix XORs is maximized.

If there are multiple solutions, you may print any.

## Note

In the first test case, the prefix XORs are [0,1,2,0][0,1,2,0], so the MEX is 33, which is the maximum possible.

In the second test case, the prefix XORs are [0,1,3,6,5,2,4,0][0,1,3,6,5,2,4,0], so the MEX is 77, which is the maximum possible.
